headline: Customer protests trigger Bangladesh Bank dissolves Islami Bank board
summary: The central bank has removed the chairman and all directors, appointing an administrator to oversee operations amid management concerns.
details: Bangladesh Bank has dissolved the board of directors of Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC, removing the chairman and all existing independent directors.
The decision comes after weeks of mounting pressure from customer protests and growing concerns regarding the bank's management and its ability to meet depositor demands.
In a notification, the central bank stated the move was made in the interest of the bank, its depositors, and the general public.
Executive Director Mohammad Jahir Hossain has been appointed as the administrator to exercise all powers and perform all responsibilities previously held by the board.
The appointment was made under Section 47(3) of the Bank Companies Act, 1991, allowing the regulator to step in and stabilize the bank's operations.
caption:
Customer protests force a major shake-up at Islami Bank. The central bank has stepped in to dissolve the board.

Bangladesh Bank has dissolved the board of directors of Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC, removing the chairman and all existing independent directors.

The decision comes after weeks of mounting pressure from customer protests and growing concerns regarding the bank's management and its ability to meet depositor demands.

In a notification, the central bank stated the move was made in the interest of the bank, its depositors, and the general public.

Executive Director Mohammad Jahir Hossain has been appointed as the administrator to exercise all powers and perform all responsibilities previously held by the board.

The appointment was made under Section 47(3) of the Bank Companies Act, 1991, allowing the regulator to step in and stabilize the bank's operations.

headline: Govt plans to bring smartphone prices down to 5,000-6,000 taka
summary: ICT Advisor Rehan Asif Azad says the government will work with manufacturers and use budget policy support to make devices more affordable.
details: Prime Minister's Advisor for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology, Rehan Asif Azad, stated that the current minimum price of a smartphone is around 10,000 taka, which acts as a barrier for many citizens.
The government plans to reduce this price to between 5,000 and 6,000 taka by discussing with manufacturers and providing necessary policy support through the national budget.
Advisor Azad also revealed that the government intends to reduce tax rates in the ICT sector every two years until 2031 to further lower costs.
He noted that the tax on SIM cards has already been withdrawn in the current budget to directly benefit general consumers.
These announcements were made during an event in Dhaka marking the launch of Grameenphone's 700 MHz spectrum, which is expected to improve 4G performance and prepare the country for 5G and AI.
Grameenphone CEO Yasir Azman stated that the 700 MHz band will significantly enhance indoor coverage and strengthen rural connectivity for millions of users.
The BTRC allocated 10 MHz of spectrum in the 700 MHz band to Grameenphone for 13 years, contributing approximately 2,200 crore taka to the state treasury.
caption:

Advisor Azad also revealed that the government intends to reduce tax rates in the ICT sector every two years until 2031 to further lower costs.

He noted that the tax on SIM cards has already been withdrawn in the current budget to directly benefit general consumers.

These announcements were made during an event in Dhaka marking the launch of Grameenphone's 700 MHz spectrum, which is expected to improve 4G performance and prepare the country for 5G and AI.

Grameenphone CEO Yasir Azman stated that the 700 MHz band will significantly enhance indoor coverage and strengthen rural connectivity for millions of users.

The BTRC allocated 10 MHz of spectrum in the 700 MHz band to Grameenphone for 13 years, contributing approximately 2,200 crore taka to the state treasury.
